environment_recovery.action: Removed obsolete downloaded shared wheel only after backup SHA256 matched; backup is agent-local, not GPU-visible. Installed runtime unchanged.

limitations: Single H100, Qwen3-0.6B BF16, seeded random token IDs, local TCP Store, test HTTP Catalog and GPFS journal; not production traffic.
Policy order is direct, KV16, teacher16, both16, with two off/on/off rounds each; not randomized and insufficient to establish statistical significance.
Native client metadata recording adds per-request overhead equally across policies.
Client timing excludes server startup, warmup, post-response writer drain and Store readback.
Publication membership alone cannot attribute latency causally. A serving batch can share capture costs across sampled and unsampled requests.
GPU capture kernel time, D2H bytes and RDMA bytes are not measured by these latency runs.

The v4 policy comparison retains group statistics and worst-request identities, but not the complete publication identity set. The final v5 collector adds that set in post-run summary, verified separately.
Historical text-gated native-client latency reports remain uncorrected; original stream events were not retained.
Production SLO, production Catalog retention and trained draft quality remain open.

source_verification.final_vs_performance_changes: Only published_trace_ids is added to the post-readback summary, plus the JSON replay unit test. Native streaming, request timing and producer modules are identical.

invalid_initial_record.interpretation: Old client initialized output_len from requested length; this is not independent proof of the actual generated count. Original SSE was not retained.

intermediate_failures.reason: Detail validation rejected zero TTFT from the old text-gated native client; no accepted comparison phases.
GPFS user quota exhausted (OSError 122), native client subprocess exited 120. report.json is zero bytes and is not a performance result.

identity_replay.command:
kubectl exec -i -n qiji job-fe1ce1dcdea6-20261001023258-master-0 -c master -- env PYTHONPATH=/gpfs/users/fuxuanwei-1/dspark-maas-lab/sglang-d2h-latency-v5/python PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /gpfs/users/fuxuanwei-1/dspark-maas-lab/venvs/capture/bin/python - <<'PY'
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
from sglang.test.training_capture_benchmark_client import summarize_requests

path = Path('/gpfs/users/fuxuanwei-1/dspark-maas-lab/experiments/d2h-latency-identity-v5/report.json')
report = json.loads(path.read_text())
assert report['status'] == 'completed'
requests = samples = phases = 0
for run in report['rounds']:
    for phase in run['phases']:
        details = phase['request_details']
        raw = Path(details['path']).read_bytes()
        assert hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == details['sha256']
        records = json.loads(raw)
        assert records['status'] == 'completed'
        ids = set(details['published_trace_ids'])
        expected = phase['readback'].get('validated_samples', 0)
        assert len(ids) == len(details['published_trace_ids']) == expected
        replay = summarize_requests(records['requests'], ids, count=64, output_len=32)
        assert replay == {key: details[key] for key in replay}
        requests += len(records['requests'])
        samples += len(ids)
        phases += 1
assert (phases, requests, samples) == (3, 192, 64)
print(json.dumps({'status': 'passed', 'phases': phases, 'requests': requests, 'published_snapshots': samples, 'record_hashes_verified': True, 'all_saved_summary_fields_reproduced': True, 'inference_requests': 0}))
PY
